papers.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.label: OPSD / Self-Distilled Reasoner
papers.summary: A problem-only student learns on its own rollouts from a self-teacher given a verified solution. The released main recipe uses a frozen base teacher and pointwise clipping. Foundational background first submitted before the recent coverage window.

papers.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning
papers.label: SDFT / Continual Learning
papers.summary: Uses a demonstration-conditioned EMA self-teacher to supervise student-generated trajectories. Reports better new-task learning and retention than SFT; the practical recipe favors forward KL despite the reverse-KL derivation. Foundational background first submitted January 27, revised August 7, 2026.

papers.title: Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents
papers.label: Skill-SD
papers.summary: Teacher-only natural-language skills summarize previous trajectories, with importance-weighted reverse KL and teacher synchronization for stability. A baseline for studying hindsight skills in multi-turn agents.

papers.title: Lightning OPD: Efficient Post-Training for Large Reasoning Models with Offline On-Policy Distillation
papers.label: Lightning OPD
papers.summary: Precomputes teacher scores over SFT rollouts and reuses them under a teacher-consistency condition. Useful for reducing distillation infrastructure cost, but it is an offline approximation to external-teacher OPD, not a new self-teacher mechanism.

papers.title: OPSDL: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Context Language Models
papers.label: OPSDL
papers.summary: Uses a short, relevant context as the self-teacher for responses generated from the full long context. Dense log-probability-ratio feedback transfers short-context competence into long-context behavior. Relevant evidence must be preserved when constructing the short context.

papers.title: MAD-OPD: Breaking the Ceiling in On-Policy Distillation via Multi-Agent Debate
papers.label: MAD-OPD
papers.summary: Multiple external teachers debate the student's current state and provide confidence-weighted supervision. A useful teacher-construction comparison, but it is multi-teacher OPD rather than the single-model OPSD setting.

papers.title: Rubric-based On-policy Distillation
papers.label: ROPD
papers.summary: Induces shared rubrics from teacher and student responses, scores rollouts with a verifier, and optimizes rubric rewards using GRPO. Supports text-only teachers and different tokenizers; distinct from verifier-free self-distillation and direct token KL matching.

papers.title: Training with Harnesses: On-Policy Harness Self-Distillation for Complex Reasoning
papers.label: OPHSD
papers.summary: Uses a harness-augmented self-teacher to internalize draft-verify and plan-solve workflows. Distinguish this from keeping a harness at deployment: the evaluated goal is to retain its benefits in the standalone model, with evidence limited to the tested harnesses.

papers.title: The Many Faces of On-Policy Distillation: Pitfalls, Mechanisms, and Fixes
papers.label: The Many Faces of OPD
papers.summary: Studies teacher-student mismatch, biased TopK reverse-KL gradients, and the distinction between transferable shared rules and instance-specific privileged information. A diagnostic companion to positive OPSD results, rather than evidence that every OPSD recipe fails.

papers.title: Respecting Self-Uncertainty in On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient LLM Reasoning
papers.label: EGRSD / CL-EGRSD
papers.summary: Combines reward-grounded update direction, likelihood-ratio magnitude, and a teacher-entropy confidence gate. The lookahead variant distinguishes persistent uncertainty from uncertainty that resolves quickly. Compare with position-based weighting rather than assuming entropy is universally reliable.

papers.title: Self-Supervised On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning Language Models
papers.label: SSOPD
papers.summary: Uses the shortest verified-correct and longest incorrect completion in a rollout group for dense correction. It avoids external solution traces, but still needs correctness verification; this separates it from fully label-free U-OPSD and CoDA.

papers.title: A Brief Overview: On-Policy Self-Distillation In Large Language Models
papers.label: Brief OPSD Overview
papers.summary: An introductory overview of the OPSD setup and design choices. Included as an orientation reference, not as a new algorithm or independent experimental validation of the original OPSD claims.

papers.title: AVSD: Adaptive-View Self-Distillation by Balancing Consensus and Teacher-Specific Privileged Signals
papers.label: AVSD
papers.summary: Combines multiple privileged views by separating their shared signal from view-specific residuals. Residuals contribute only when aligned with the consensus, offering a different answer to teacher inconsistency than using a single richer context.

papers.title: When Are Teacher Tokens Reliable? Position-Weighted On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning
papers.label: PW-OPSD
papers.summary: A branch-viability diagnostic motivates increasing token-position weights while retaining OPSD's rollout and clipped forward-KL target. The reported local uncertainty predictors are weak in its diagnostic, making it an important comparison for entropy-based recipes.

papers.title: Tailoring Teaching to Aptitude: Direction-Adaptive Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
papers.label: DASD
papers.summary: Routes the direction of teacher supervision by token entropy: attraction at low entropy and repulsion at high entropy. A more interventionist response to lost exploration than merely clipping or downweighting teacher signals.

papers.title: Beyond Imitation: Reflective On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
papers.label: ROSD
papers.summary: A self-reflector contrasts successful and failed rollouts, extracts a corrective idea, and locates the first erroneous sentence. Distillation skips the valid prefix of diagnosed failures, targeting correction while seeking to preserve reasoning diversity.

papers.title: Internalize the Temperature: On-Policy Self-Distillation as Policy Reheater for Reinforcement Learning
papers.label: TS-OPSD / Policy Reheater
papers.summary: Distills a temperature-smoothed copy of an entropy-collapsed policy back into itself before continuing RL. Its teacher advantage is a distribution transformation, not a privileged answer; the metadata first-submission date is May 30 despite the June arXiv identifier.

papers.title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
papers.label: Self-Harness
papers.summary: Improves the external harness through weakness mining, candidate edits, and regression-based acceptance while keeping model weights fixed. It can supply better training scaffolds, but does not itself perform token-level on-policy self-distillation.

papers.title: HERO: Hindsight-Enhanced Reflection from Environment Observations for Agentic Self-Distillation
papers.label: HERO
papers.summary: Compresses completed interactions into local hindsight diagnoses grounded in the next environment observation. Re-scores original action tokens with turn-specific hints, addressing the mismatch between whole-trajectory feedback and the agent's local decision.

papers.title: RLCSD: Reinforcement Learning with Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.label: RLCSD
papers.summary: Contrasts correct-hint and wrong-hint teacher signals to reduce privilege-induced style drift, then uses the contrast for verifier-grounded credit modulation. This is a close companion to SIPO and the thinking-collapse diagnostics.

papers.title: Rubric-Guided Self-Distillation: Post-Training Without Rubric Verifiers
papers.label: RGSD
papers.summary: A frozen rubric-conditioned copy of the base model supervises student prefixes using clipped JSD (beta 0.5), with no training-time judge. Thinking-token masking limits rubric leakage. The study does not compare JSD against KL under matched conditions.

papers.title: Rethinking Reward Supervision: Rubric-Conditioned Self-Distillation
papers.label: RCSD
papers.summary: Learns a rubric generator using answer-privileged OPSD, then conditions a self-teacher on its rubrics to train a reasoner. Its Qwen3-8B loss ablation favors forward KL on average (70.6) over reverse KL (69.9) and JSD (69.6); individual benchmarks differ.

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Sampled Demonstrations Reduces Output Diversity
papers.label: Sampled Demonstrations & Diversity
papers.summary: Analyzes how conditioning on sampled correct demonstrations can compound existing mode preferences. Graph path-finding and science QA experiments motivate evaluating pass@k and functional diversity alongside average success.

papers.title: OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.label: OPID
papers.summary: Extracts episode-level and critical-step hindsight skills from completed on-policy trajectories. Re-scoring the original responses with those skills supplies a dense auxiliary advantage alongside outcome-based RL.

papers.title: Denser $\neq$ Better: Limits of On-Policy Self-Distillation for Continual Post-Training
papers.label: Denser ≠ Better
papers.summary: Tests SDPO in continual post-training and links failures to teacher instability, drift, and reinforced artifacts. On-policy data and dense feedback do not automatically prevent forgetting; conclusions are scoped to the evaluated protocols.

papers.title: Purified OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation Without Losing How to Think
papers.label: Purified OPSD
papers.summary: Uses a reference-only teacher to estimate the shortcut component of privileged supervision, then forms a PMI-based residual target anchored to a clean base distribution. Closely related to RLCSD's attempt to separate useful corrections from context-induced style changes.

papers.title: dOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Diffusion Language Models
papers.label: dOPSD
papers.summary: Constructs the teacher's privilege from a later, more decoded state of the student's own diffusion trajectory. Extends the self-teaching idea beyond autoregressive LMs without relying on an externally supplied solution.

papers.title: Rethinking On-Policy Self-Distillation for Thinking Models
papers.label: Rethinking OPSD for Thinking Models
papers.summary: Reports degradation in five thinking models and examines suppressed self-correction at high-entropy branching points. Essential context for interpreting gains obtained with non-thinking training and thinking-enabled evaluation.

papers.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Thinking Collapse in On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.label: AD-OPSD / Thinking Collapse
papers.summary: Diagnoses suppression of epistemic tokens at uncertain decision forks and selectively anchors risky updates to a frozen base prior. Provides a targeted safeguard to compare against clipping, PMI purification, and entropy routing.

papers.title: Demystifying On-Policy Distillation: Roles, Pathologies, and Regulations
papers.label: Demystifying OPD
papers.summary: Studies teacher-student mismatch and length exploitation in OPD, with clipping and log-scale compression as signal controls. Relevant to OPSD implementation and evaluation, but broader external-teacher findings should not be assumed to transfer unchanged.

papers.title: SEED: Self-Evolving On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.label: SEED
papers.summary: First teaches the policy to produce hindsight skills, then uses the improving policy as both actor and skill analyzer during joint RL and distillation. Its initial skill-training stage should be distinguished from a method that needs no external supervision at any stage.

papers.title: DREvo: Distilling Recalibrated Historical Experience for Harness Self-Evolution
papers.label: DREvo
papers.summary: Reassesses historical evidence and turns it into search guidance for harness changes. The optimized artifact is the harness, so its use of 'distillation' should not be confused with OPSD updates to model weights.

papers.title: Flux-OPD: On-Policy Distillation with Evolving Contexts
papers.label: Flux-OPD
papers.summary: Handles evolving contexts using an anchored contextual difference signal and conflict-dependent weighting. A useful extension for open-ended tasks where a fixed privileged context becomes stale; broader context distillation rather than only answer-conditioned OPSD.

papers.title: Group-Reflective Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.label: GRSD
papers.summary: Contrasts the policy's reflections on successful and failed rollouts to construct group-level guidance. It redistributes trajectory advantages across turns while preserving the verifier-determined update direction.

papers.title: $\beta$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
papers.label: β-OPSD
papers.summary: Derives a KL-regularized policy-optimization family and realizes its target through reference-teacher logit interpolation. Adds explicit reference strength and return-to-go credit; closely related to SR-OPSD's target-construction question.

papers.title: Mitigating Rubric Interference in LLM Judges via On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.label: SARA
papers.summary: Aligns joint rubric judgments to single-rubric EMA-teacher analysis with symmetric JSD, plus a separate full-context structural-preservation term. Improves judge consistency; isolated judgments are not guaranteed correct. Primarily instruct-mode evaluation, with limited thinking-mode transfer.

papers.title: AgentOPSD: Recursive Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.label: AgentOPSD
papers.summary: Aggregates token-level teacher-student gaps into turn evidence and recursively updates a success-belief proxy. The resulting weights refine temporal credit without a learned critic; the Bayesian interpretation uses a computable proxy for unavailable outcome-conditioned policies.

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
papers.label: U-OPSD
papers.summary: Builds a pseudo-reference from majority agreement and distills along disagreeing completions, without gold answers or an external teacher. The paper's limitations emphasize canonicalizable answers, base-model competence, and smaller gains in thinking mode.

papers.title: Learning from Consensus and Disagreement: Unsupervised On-Policy Self-Distillation with Minority-Trajectory Contrast
papers.label: CoDA
papers.summary: Uses answer consensus to condition a self-teacher and adds reference-anchored, KTO-style calibration of minority trajectories. Unlike U-OPSD's correction of disagreeing completions, it also collects fresh student trajectories for distribution alignment.

papers.title: Privileged Solutions or Context-Induced Teacher Behavior? Dissecting On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.label: OP²SD
papers.summary: Replaces the paired solution with a worked example from another problem while preserving the OPSD training setup. Tests whether gains require target-specific answers or can arise from teacher behavior induced by context; arbitrary context is not established as equally useful.

papers.title: SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.label: SR-OPSD
papers.summary: Combines a geometric target anchored to the frozen initial policy with forward Rényi projection. Target construction and projection interact; its fixed-context analysis does not establish stability of the entire evolving training process.

papers.title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.label: LOPD
papers.summary: Learns continuous privileged context from retrieved experiences rather than prescribing a natural-language skill format. A privilege-margin constraint prevents the teacher advantage from collapsing during context learning.

papers.title: Trust Is Not Enough: Influence Calibration for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Agentic RL
papers.label: ICSD
papers.summary: Weights privileged self-distillation by its estimated compatibility with the current RL objective, while preserving auxiliary-loss mass within each turn. Teacher confidence alone is treated as insufficient evidence that an update will help the task.

papers.title: DualOPSD: Adaptive Privileged Teachers for On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.label: DualOPSD
papers.summary: Alternates student learning with teacher adaptation on the same rollout. Its own limitations report scale-dependent accuracy effects, one training seed, and a reversal at 1.7B; reduced teacher-student KL is not by itself evidence of better reasoning.

papers.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
papers.label: TTPO
papers.summary: Routes majority-agreeing rollouts to distillation and disagreeing rollouts to a grouped-RL penalty, with token selection in both branches. Particularly relevant to label-free test-time adaptation, whose evaluation protocol differs from ordinary held-out post-training.

papers.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation
papers.label: RISE
papers.summary: Extrapolates the model's own RLVR progress in weights or logits to synthesize an improving teacher. Removes privileged-context dependence while retaining outcome supervision. Compare with B-OPSD's explicitly trained future teacher and restarted student.

papers.title: Beyond Verified Answers: Solver-Informed Self-Distillation for Bootstrapping Operations Research Language Models
papers.label: SOLID
papers.summary: Uses solver artifacts and majority groups of executed candidate programs as pseudo-references for operations-research formulations. Connects label-free reference construction to a domain with executable feedback; it is not supervision-free in the sense of having no environment.

papers.title: What Does Privileged Information Add to On-Policy Self-Distillation?
papers.label: What Does Privileged Information Add?
papers.summary: Uses matched reference-free and six-view controls to separate distillation gains from the marginal benefit of privileged references. Highlights dependence on training and evaluation reasoning modes, directly complementing the OP²SD intervention.

papers.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.label: RetireOPD
papers.summary: Trains a skill-conditioned teacher, jointly trains the skill-free student with RL and distillation, then retires the teacher when transfer stalls and the student reaches a competence threshold. Adds a training-stage perspective to teacher quality.

papers.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
papers.label: Harness-Zero
papers.summary: A harnessing agent reviews and corrects student proposals to collect trajectories, followed by SFT. It transfers behavior from an evolved harness to a fixed target harness, rather than matching privileged teacher token distributions in an OPSD loop.

papers.title: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
papers.label: GUI-SD-v2
papers.summary: First improves privilege-following ability, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory guidance for multi-turn GUI agents. Extends teacher-quality and temporal-credit questions to GUI interaction.

papers.title: Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning
papers.label: DCE + SRCL
papers.summary: Refreshes the detached privileged teacher from the current student each round and adds cross-entropy on shorter, verified self-rewrites. Forward KL leads its 8B loss comparison; non-thinking-mode, selected-checkpoint results do not establish frontier thinking-model gains.

papers.title: TISD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Trajectory Intervention
papers.label: TISD
papers.summary: Uses teacher disagreement to choose a branch token, forces that action, and returns suffix generation to the student before distillation. It changes the visited training states, not just the weight assigned to existing tokens; include regeneration cost in comparisons.

papers.title: Teach Yourself Where to Look: On-Policy Attention Self-Distillation for Reasoning
papers.label: OPASD
papers.summary: Adds attention supervision to token matching, projecting the privileged teacher's attention onto positions visible to the student before normalization. A direct complement to PR-OPD's hidden-state alignment and LOPD's learned privileged context.

papers.title: PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.label: PR-OPD
papers.summary: After an RL warm start, the model writes hindsight skills and aligns projected student hidden states with its privileged teacher. This tests whether useful guidance resides in representations even when token probabilities barely change.

papers.title: Know Thyself, Teach Thyself: Internal Information Flow for Selective Self-Distillation
papers.label: InFlow
papers.summary: Retrieves useful sources from calibrated hidden-state trajectories, then selects examples by the change in teacher answer beliefs after retrieval. Connects retrieval quality and sample selection to on-policy distillation without gold labels or a stronger teacher.

papers.title: SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.label: SIPO
papers.summary: Contrasts teacher contexts built from a reference answer and rollout-group mistakes to obtain dense token credit while retaining task-reward optimization. Especially close to RLCSD; unlike purely group-relative outcome advantages, it can provide a signal in all-failure groups.

papers.title: Train Ahead, Distill Back: Bootstrapping On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.label: B-OPSD
papers.summary: Temporarily trains ahead to obtain a future teacher, freezes it, restarts the student, and distills on the restarted student's trajectories. Studies both answer-available and answer-free pathways; the lookahead stage adds training work that belongs in cost comparisons.

papers.title: Harness-Aware Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
papers.label: HAD
papers.summary: Distills a larger teacher into a smaller agent that retains the same harness. Adds an action preference from teacher responses with versus without harness information and rejects invalid preferences. Its deployment premise differs from removing the harness.

papers.title: Outcome-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.label: OG-OPSD
papers.summary: Uses forward KL on complete correct trajectories and reverse KL on selected prefixes of incorrect ones. Cumulative teacher entropy helps choose the supervised prefix, connecting outcome correctness to both objective and token selection.
